title: DayZero capacity tiling and demand-priced matrix
body:
Summary:
This sheet captures a compact, deployable approach for aligning short-window (Day0-90) capacity tiling to price movements and headcount lag. It is intentionally tactical — meant for an operational finance + infra sync to set token-price triggers, hiring lead times, and commit-tiling rules for Dedicated and Hosted tiers.

Key ideas (one-liners):
- Capacity tiling: slice reserved GPU capacity into smaller commit "tiles" so we can add or retire capacity weekly rather than monthly; reduces overcommit risk and lets pricing act as the governor.
- Demand-priced matrix: map price bands to capacity tile actions (buy/hold/shed) and hiring triggers.
- Day-zero cushion: maintain a small 14-day burst reserve funded from operating buffer to handle token spikes without breaking SLOs.
- Hire lag function: assume 8–10 weeks time-to-full-productivity for infra/ops hires; use contractor layer for 0–8 week coverage.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Token price sensitivity: a 10% drop in average per-token price increases self-serve demand by 12% in 60 days (elasticity -1.2).
- GPU price / spot availability: regional spot capacity shocks increase GPU-hour cost by 35% for up to 3 weeks.
- Quantization path: enabling 8-bit quantization reduces token GPU-hours by ~22% but introduces a potential 0.5–1.0% quality drift on completion-sensitive prompts.
- Baseline token growth: mid-case +6% month-over-month.
- Hiring: on-payroll FTE productivity ramp = 70% at week 4, 90% at week 8, 100% at week 12.

Compact scenario table (monthly view; summary lines for tile sizing). Columns: Month, Scenario, TokenVolume (M), AvgPrice ($/k tokens), GPU-hours, ReserveTiles, FTEs (ops+infra).

Notes on table: ReserveTiles = number of pre-warmed small commit blocks (typical block = 0.5 p4d-week equivalent). We recommend starting with 2 tiles in baseline for June.

Headcount phasing (compact):
- Hiring plan Q3 start: 2 infra SRE hires (L4), 1 infra engineer (L3), 1 finance analyst (L3) as primary hires to support tiling automation and realtime costing.
- Contractor layer: 0.6 FTE-equivalent (fractional infra contractor) for first 8–10 weeks.
- Cost estimate: blended fully-burdened cost: FTE L3 = $18k/mo, L4 = $28k/mo, contractor equivalent = $24k/mo (short term).

Pricing sensitivity matrix (decision rules):
- Trigger A (Price falls >= 12% vs baseline over 14d): deploy 1 extra reserve tile, pause non-essential Dedicated expansion, run market-price routing to cheaper model variants.
- Trigger B (Token volume rises >= 20% vs baseline over 7d): enable burst-to-dedicated policy, increase pre-warm tiles +1 for 21 days, open contractor slots immediately.
- Trigger C (GPU-hour spot cost > +30% for 3 consecutive days): shift high-latency batch jobs to offline queue, throttle low-priority embeddings by token-budget gating.

Micro-sensitivity outputs (examples):
- If AvgPrice drops from $18.5 -> $16.0 (13.5%): expected token delta +16% in 60d, GPU-hours +12%, revenue per token down ~13.5%; net margin impact -6.5 p.p (approx).
- If quantization rollout to 8-bit applied to 40% of traffic: GPU-hours drop ~8.8% total; headcount demand stable but cost per-token decreases. Watch quality regression signal and tie to evals.

Cash flow sketch (90-day rolling):
- Day0 buffer: $1.2M operating cushion earmarked for DayZero reserve (covers 14-day burst at 150% baseline).
- Recommended reallocation: shift $250k from long-lead hiring cushion into cloud pre-pay tiles to buy optionality this quarter.

Actionable runbook (first 30 days):
1) Finance + Infra triage (within 72h): accept tiling pilot params; assign infra lead to automation ticket (GH PR linked above).
2) Create telemetry dashboard: daily tile utilization, pre-warm latency, price vs volume curves. Owner: Eva Morales.
3) Kick contractor sourcing: 1 infra contractor (0.6 FTE) to cover 8–10 week lag. Owner: People Ops + Samir.
4) Implement pricing triggers in Console as alert rules (Trigger A/B/C). Owner: Product - Hosted API.

Open questions / risks:
- Quality-vs-cost tradeoffs for quantization: need 500 prompt-pair evals targeted at high-sensitivity customers before broad rollout.
- Spot market correlation risk across regions: synchronized spot failures could erode tiling benefits; consider multi-region tile diversification.
- Billing/commit smoothing complexity: weekly tiling increases billing touchpoints; Finance needs a light reconciliation flow.

Appendix: small sample math for baseline month (June):
- Baseline tokens: 120M; AvgPrice $18.5 per 1k -> revenue = 120,000 * 18.5 = $2.22M (approx).
- GPU-hours: 4,200; average GPU-hour cost blended = $9.5 -> infra cost = $39.9k; gross margin before headcount/ops = revenue - infra = ~$2.18M.

Next steps / proposed meeting cadence:
- Weekly 30-min Finance + Infra sync for first 8 weeks to monitor tiling and triggers (standup notes captured to FIN-3212).
- Deep review at 45 days: re-evaluate tile size and reserve funding.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working sheet intended to be converted into a 2-tab workbook (1: numbers, 2: sensitivity dashboard). If accepted, I'll spin up the sheet and hand off to Eva to instrument the dashboards.

-- Aisha
